editorNote: Today's edition runs from a leaked Apple app to a critical audit of AI-found vulnerabilities, a startup shutting down, and a patent fight that ended a driver. Several items are single-source claims and are labeled that way.

stories.headline: Apple's 'Harbor' app, found by a leaker, would turn Macs into a private local AI server
stories.summary: 9to5Mac reports leaker Aaron Perris found evidence of Harbor, an app that runs open-weight models on Apple silicon and can link Macs over Thunderbolt 5 to pool memory. It is reportedly in private preview under the Claris brand.
stories.whyItMatters: If real, Apple is packaging local model serving with no command-line setup; it is a leak, not an announcement.

sourceLinks.title: 9to5Mac: Apple has new Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy

stories.headline: VulnCheck says Anthropic's Glasswing ledger shows findings far outpacing fixes
stories.summary: VulnCheck counts 442 Anthropic-attributed CVEs (about 0.5% of this year's total), with 37,966 findings logged but only 217 marked fixed. In curl's case, 19 of 34 published reports were not vulnerabilities.
stories.whyItMatters: The critique argues triage burden is landing on maintainers; it is one vendor's analysis of Anthropic's own ledger.

stories.headline: Val Town is winding down, with read-only mode starting Dec. 10 and open-sourcing planned for Feb. 1
stories.summary: Founder Steve Krouse said Val Town couldn't compete in cloud computing. New signups ended Nov. 10, all other services end Jan. 10, 2027, and annual prepayers get a partial refund.
stories.whyItMatters: Users have about two months to migrate; the company points to Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify and Render guides.

sourceLinks.title: Val Town blog: Val Town is winding down

stories.headline: A Google engineer says AI agents flagged a possibly unmapped Maya site in public lidar data
stories.summary: Pietro Miotti says agents reviewed about 1,200 km² of lidar and flagged a hilltop site with a plaza and an oval pyramid. Mexico's INAH says it has no registered site there; the author stresses the claim is unconfirmed and he is not an archaeologist.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a self-reported result awaiting archaeological verification.

stories.headline: Synaptics' patent threats led a developer to shelve a Linux DisplayLink driver
stories.summary: LWN reports Mike Lothian, who wrote the LLM-assisted Rust driver Vino, received a cease-and-desist citing 125 patents and later claim charts for two UK patents. He removed his repository and will keep the driver local.
stories.whyItMatters: The case shows patent exposure for clean-room drivers that OIN's protections do not cover, since codecs are excluded.

sourceLinks.title: LWN: Synaptics patent claims stop work on DisplayLink drivers

stories.headline: Toyota revives Scion with a kei truck, but it is a low-speed fleet pilot due in late 2027
stories.summary: The Autopian says the KEI-01 is a rebadged Toyota Pixis built in Indiana, limited to under 25 mph and roads posted under 35 mph. Toyota will sell it directly, starting with a fleet-focused pilot.
stories.whyItMatters: Wider availability is undetermined, and the speed limit restricts it to farm, warehouse and urban delivery work.

sourceLinks.title: The Autopian: Scion is back and is going to sell a kei truck in America
